core_obligations: Setup and first reduction: choose a surjective smooth $\mathcal{U} \to \mathcal{X}$ representable by a scheme; base change of higher direct images (cited Sheaves on Stacks lemma) plus assumption (2) on the smooth projection and assumption (3) replace $\mathcal{Y} \to \mathcal{X}$ by $\mathcal{U} \times_\mathcal{X} \mathcal{Y} \to \mathcal{U}$; Zariski locality via (3) makes $\mathcal{X}$ affine (proof lines 486-507).

Spectral sequence step: choose surjective smooth $g : \mathcal{V} \to \mathcal{Y}$ with $\mathcal{V}$ affine-representable and run the $E_2^{p,q} = R^q(f \circ g_p)_* g_p^*\mathcal{F} \Rightarrow R^{p+q} f_* \mathcal{F}$ spectral sequence (first quadrant, cited); the $g_p$ are smooth so $g_p^*\mathcal{F}$ is in $\mathcal{M}_{\mathcal{V}_p}$ by (2), reducing to the morphisms $\mathcal{V}_p \to \mathcal{X}$ (proof lines 509-529).

Upgrade $\mathcal{Y}$: qcqs permanence makes $\mathcal{V}_p$ qcqs and the stack diagonal makes them algebraic spaces; restart the argument: spaces have scheme diagonals so $\mathcal{V}_p$ are qcqs schemes; schemes have separated diagonals so $\mathcal{V}_p$ are separated; separated schemes have affine diagonals so $\mathcal{V}_p$ are affine, where assumption (4) applies (proof lines 531-580).
proof_roadmap: Reduce the base to an affine scheme via base change and smooth-locality.
Cover the source smoothly and reduce to the $\check{\mathrm{C}}$ech terms via the spectral sequence.
Iterate the covering argument to upgrade the source through space, scheme, separated scheme, affine scheme.
difficulty_reason: The proof is a five-step iterated reduction driven by the smooth-covering spectral sequence: make $\mathcal{X}$ a scheme, then affine; make $\mathcal{Y}$ an algebraic space, then a scheme, then separated, then affine, each restart of the smooth-covering argument upgrading $\mathcal{Y}$ one step via the representability of diagonals (stack diagonal by algebraic spaces, space diagonal by schemes, scheme diagonal separated, separated diagonal affine), landing in assumption (4).
